Model Text Summary:
A biographical account celebrating Dr. Bibha Chowdhuri (1913–1991), a pioneering Indian nuclear physicist. In the 1930s and 1940s, working at the Bose Institute in Kolkata and later at the University of Manchester under Nobel Laureate Patrick Blackett, she conducted groundbreaking research on cosmic rays and subatomic particles (pi-mesons). Erwin Schrödinger nominated her for a Nobel Prize. She became the first woman scientist at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR). In 2019, the International Astronomical Union permanently named a star 'Bibha' in her honor.
